facts.item: tingling pain in the sole of the right foot
aliases: pins and needles in the foot
facts.text: I get a tingling pain in the sole of my right foot.
It's been happening for the last 6 weeks.

facts.item: foot pain: what brings it on
facts.text: It comes on during exercise, when I raise my foot above chest level.

facts.item: calf cramps: what brings them on
facts.text: It happens when I use the incline feature on my treadmill.
The pain goes away after a few minutes of rest.
I don't have any other symptoms.
I've had type 2 diabetes for 8 years.
I've been taking metformin for my diabetes for the past 8 years.
I smoke two packs a day, and have for 34 years.
I started exercising regularly 2 months ago.

findings.name: straight-leg raise test
findings.result: Induces pallor and tingling pain in the right foot, without back pain.

findings.name: peripheral pulses
findings.result: Femoral pulses palpable; right pedal pulses absent.

findings.name: ankle-brachial index
findings.result: Right: reduced, indicative of peripheral artery disease.

findings.name: Doppler ultrasound of the right leg
findings.result: Reduced blood flow and stenosis in the femoropopliteal artery segment.

f007: 'The pain subsides after a few minutes of rest' follows the calf-cramp sentence but may cover both complaints; kept as a standalone fact for both.
f011: '34-year history of smoking two packs per day' is read as current smoking.
f001: System 'neurological' follows the patient's description (tingling); the cause is vascular.

x003.source_text: Induces pallor and tingling pain in the right foot, without back pain

x005.source_text: Femoral pulses palpable, right pedal pulses absent

x007.source_text: Reduced, indicative of peripheral artery disease

x008.source_text: Reduced blood flow and stenosis in the femoropopliteal artery segment

x003: The source calls this a straight-leg raise, but the finding (pallor and foot pain on elevation, no back pain) is the leg-elevation (Buerger) response; 'Buerger test' and 'leg elevation test' are aliases so either request gets it. System set to cardiovascular for that reason.
x007: Only the right ABI is reported, with no numeric value.

leakage.reason: The Doppler result states the gold diagnosis (stenosis in the femoropopliteal segment); kept because it is the imaging answer.
The ABI result names peripheral artery disease, a broader category containing the gold diagnosis; kept as the source interpretation.

source_issues: The 'straight leg raise test' result describes elevation pallor, which is Buerger's test, not a nerve-root test.
No temperature or respiratory rate is given.
The ankle-brachial index and fasting glucose are qualitative ('Reduced', 'Elevated') with no values.
notes: Foot pain and calf cramps keep separate triggers (raising the foot above chest level during exercise; treadmill incline). Relief with rest is a standalone fact because it is not clear which pain it refers to.
Diabetes is a prior diagnosis the patient knows, so its name stays in the patient text.
Finding names and aliases avoid the gold words 'artery' and 'stenosis'; 'arterial' is used where needed.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate a 55-year-old man presenting with foot pain and cramping during exercise, and diagnose the underlying condition.
